items.title: Delhi High Court denies anticipatory bail to builder Nayan Raheja in money laundering case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday dismissed the anticipatory bail application filed by builder Nayan N Raheja in a money laundering case filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). Justice Amit Bansal rejected Raheja's anticipatory bail plea. A detailed order is awaited. ED is probing a case involving the alleged diversion of funds collected from homebuyers of projects developed by Raheja Developers. It is alleged that nearly ₹2,699 crore was collected from homebuyers, of which around ₹1,353 crore was allegedly diverted through various accounts, group entities and related transactions. The agency alleged that Raheja repeatedly failed to appear before investigators despite summons issued under Section 50 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and undertakings given before courts to cooperate with the probe. Senior Advocate Vikas Pahwa with advocates Sandeep Kapur, Manmeet Kaur, Irfan Muzamil, Jasmeet Singh, Rishabh Munjal, Priyal Jain, Kholi Rakuzhuro and Kunal Kochar appeared for Nayan Raheja. Advocates Rajat Nair, Sarthak Maan and Dhruv Pande represented the ED.

Pertinently, the Delhi Police on October 13 told the Delhi High Court that the decision was taken based on the Supreme Court's order of October 9. However, the Central government today denied the same. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi questioned the Centre, "[Was it de-notified] Because of some oral observations of the Court, or was there an application of mind with regard to the site and its efficacy in being used as a common protest site?" CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Union, replied, "The Court's judgment is not the basis of the decision. The committee was constituted much before. The committee has given a detailed report." SG Tushar Mehta Senior Advocate Mukta Gupta , appearing for the petitioner, stressed on the fundamental rights of citizens to protest peacefully. items.title: Delhi High Court rules it can execute commercial decrees below ₹2 crore if original suit was within its jurisdiction
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that it can execute a decree arising from a commercial suit even if the amount sought to be recovered is below its ₹2 crore pecuniary jurisdiction threshold, provided the original suit was within its jurisdiction [Ozone SPA Vs Co-incept] Justice Subramonium Prasad held that a court does not lose its jurisdiction to execute a decree merely because the decretal amount falls below its pecuniary threshold. " The contention that alteration in pecuniary limit of the court which passed the decree would also take away the power of such Court to execute the said decree cannot be accepted ," the Court observed. Justice Subramonium Prasad The ruling came in an execution petition filed by Ozone Spa Private Limited against Co-Incept Hospitality Private Limited and others, seeking enforcement of a ₹1.19 crore decree passed in July 2018. The dispute arose from a franchise agreement executed in December 2013, under which Co-Incept Hospitality was permitted to operate a gym, spa and salon under the Ozone brand at Rajouri Garden in Delhi. It said that only 45 of its 303 stations were closed for entry and exit on October 10, after the Supreme Court on October 9 ordered that there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of metro trains. DMRC Chairperson D Thara has also tendered an "unconditional apology" in an affidavit filed in response to a contempt notice issued on October 11. On October 9, a Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant took up an oral mentioning against Delhi Police communications. These had asked DMRC to shut entry and exit gates at 57 stations and reduce train frequency. The Court said that the notifications appeared "overreaching, as they impose a complete ban upon essential public transportation." The Bench had clarified there "shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains". It said that any regulated arrangement should be "widely publicised". items.title: Jailer 2: Nelson-Rajini team up for more of the same, but with less fun
items.summary: Director Nelson Dileepkumar’s Jailer 2 may exhaust you, then lull you into a stupor with its bottomless supply of excesses. Sequels mostly work if the previous film possessed some internal logic to continue from. But while Jailer (2023) was a quirky and fun watch , it was also full of laughable plot holes that didn’t come with enough stakes to set up a worthy second instalment. And now, possibly, a third. In Jailer 2, Rajinikanth returns as ‘Tiger’ Muthuvel Pandian, a retired warden who once terrorised inmates at Tihar jail. The first film established Muthu (a callback to the 1995 Rajini film of the same name) as a man whose influence reaches far beyond that of any prison warden and spans several states. Jailer 2 carries that forward along with his skill to hide in plain sight. Working as a driver for a bumbling small-time thug, Muthu continues his crusade against an idol-smuggling mafia. The film builds up to a face-off between him and Bodhi Kalpak (SJ Suryah). Suryah’s trademark theatrics are a few shades more muted in Jailer 2 , which makes Bodhi one of the more interesting characters.
